findings.where: resources/workflow-graph/workflow-graph.v1.json (t_352–t_369; cond_258, cond_262, cond_265, cond_274) vs 01-core-flows.md §7 and docs/contracts/epic-staging.md §1–§6
findings.what: The workflow graph is a candidate member, and its digest is pinned into task identity, but its Epic integration path is still the old order that round 1 flagged: ticket_join → accept → integrate (a self-loop over transitions until 'все Tickets integrated') → aggregate_verify → cleanup ('все epic-критерии PASS — cleanup'). It has no staging step, no acceptance of the verified staging identity, no single target CAS after aggregate PASS and no post-CAS read-back. So either the target moves before aggregate verification, which breaks the invariant §7 calls the reason staging exists, or the Epic reaches cleanup/done without the target ever moving. The fix was made in the prose only, not in the state machine the daemon runs. This blocks.

The graph has no delivery-profile branch: no step where the host opens a PR or queues the merge instead of moving the branch, and no step that waits for the profile's completion predicate. `completion_predicate_unmet` is neither a park reason in the graph nor an entry in the refusal vocabulary, and none of epic-staging's 11 closed classes (for example staging_moved_after_pass, post_cas_mismatch, acceptance_stale) appears in the graph or the vocabulary. The terminal state that §7 step 10 adds so that a PR or merge-queue Epic can finish exists only in prose, and those refusals have no step to park at.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §7 preamble and step 7; workflow-graph.v1.json cond_262; epic-staging.md §6
findings.what: §7 contradicts itself on how the target moves. The preamble and cond_262 describe an authorization over 'ordered ref transitions' with a completed prefix and the remaining transitions after a partial CAS. Step 7 and epic-staging require exactly one target CAS whose expected old value equals the recorded base, and with a single CAS there is no partial prefix to keep.

In the code, REVIEWER_ORDER is ['gpt','kimi','grok'] and never offers Opus, while the §6 table routes Codex, Grok, Kimi and Human authorship to Opus. Families also arrive as caller-supplied strings: the code maps anthropic→'claude' where the partition calls the family 'opus', and it never consults family-partition.v1.json. The claim that 'the family is derived from the model, not the harness' is therefore enforced only for REQUIRED_PANEL. An author label such as 'cursor' or 'meta' excludes no reviewer.

Nothing evaluates the rule that Lead must come from a family outside every author and fixer, and nothing evaluates the rule that a Supplementary seat's Critical or High cannot block on its own. A search of src/ and scripts/ finds no Lead selection and no 'supplementary'; panel.mjs and the finding gate treat all four seats the same. Both are load-bearing rules that exist only as description.

The partition files Meta's muse-spark-1.3(-contributor) under the 'kimi' family. Separately, the §3 seat table still gives GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3 and Opus 5 routes without the 'historical' marker that 02 §9 attaches to the same routes, and 02 §9 says the partition refuses three of those four routes.

findings.where: package §1 'What is being delivered'; 02-architecture.md §2 (autoskd) and §3; 04-decisions.md ADR-023/ADR-025
findings.what: The package says the pinned series 'supplies' ADR-023 and ADR-025, but no patch in compat/autosk/patches implements a signed UserDecisionRecord, user-presence nonce, consumed_nonce/authority/dependency/intent/integration_authorization/result heads, appendIntentEvent, authorityGuard, integrateApproved, orchestrateChildBatch, step-capability metadata CAS or gate-result receipts (a grep of all 49 patches for these names finds nothing), so the user-authority chain and workflow custody that the design rests on do not exist in the daemon it declares it runs on.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §3–§4 ('MVP preflight forbids any model workflow if any primitive is absent'); src/host/daemon-preflight.mjs:22
findings.what: REQUIRED_DAEMON_CAPABILITIES lists only 'task.creation-binding' (ADR-014), and patch 0013's meta.capabilities reports only that capability, so the preflight cannot refuse a daemon that lacks the ADR-023/025 primitives, and 'mutable fallback forbidden' is not enforced by the mechanism the text names.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §2 Git and §3 patch mapping ('custody helper and its protocol (0016–0022, 0024)'); src/git/ref-custody-helper.ts
findings.what: Patches 0016–0022/0024 implement the store-lock helper (cmd/autosk-store-lock, daemon/core/src/store/creation.ts), not the Git ref-custody helper, and no patch touches refs/autosk; src/git/ref-custody-helper.ts does not exist, so the sole-writer ref custody, separate-account boundary, peer-credential check and denied-probe bootstrap are only described, with no code in the repo or the series.

The deferral list does not say that the ADR-023/025 daemon primitives and the Git ref-custody helper are absent, while it does name much smaller gaps (the Sonar pilot, the missing class-to-mutant mapping), so a reader of §5 would take the missing core primitives to be delivered.

findings.where: package §5 fault matrix F017–F020; 02-architecture.md §2 planning publication adapter
findings.what: The planning-publication fault groups run in the extension's fault harness against Git directly; because no helper or daemon custody path exists, they cannot show that the helper-mediated CAS or the separate-account boundary behaves as the design says.

findings.where: docs/contracts/autobuild-run.md, reflect-cost-watch.md, housekeeping.md, debate.md, walkthrough.md (Status lines, debate.md:95) vs resources/program-capabilities/matrix.v1.json and docs/program-capability-matrix.md
findings.what: The matrix classifies #28, #29, #30, #31 and #33 as planned_after_v1 and says they do not block release, but each of those five contracts says its runtime 'remain[s] `required_for_v1`'. The candidate therefore gives two opposite answers to the one question the owner asked the classification to settle: what blocks the autonomous MVP.

Issue #47 (SonarQube) is outside the pinned #3–#39 inventory, yet its contract calls its adapter, pilot and webhook receiver `required_for_v1` and adds two classes to the #14 registry. The matrix rule forbids an issue outside the inventory from becoming a v1 or release blocker without a successor matrix version, and matrix.v1 is still the only version, so this is exactly the silent promotion the owner's rule was written to stop.

The 'kimi' family lists Meta's muse-spark-1.3 and muse-spark-1.3-contributor models, so the required Intent route (meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor) counts as the Kimi family. The same file says family is a property of the model and not a label, and relabeling a different vendor's model to fill the fourth family weakens the four-distinct-families guarantee the owner asked the panel to have. This is not the product-roster difference dispositioned as debt 8b.

02-architecture.md §9 marks the GPT-5.6 Sol / Grok 4.6 / Kimi K3 / Opus 5 routes as historical and says the live roster comes only from REQUIRED_PANEL. 01-core-flows.md §3 still presents those same routes as the panel, with no historical marker, so the two load-bearing documents disagree about who sits on the panel.

The Arena flow presents Debate as a selectable path with its own roster and gates and never says that Debate is inactive in v1. The matrix obligation for #31 before #39 was to mark Debate inactive_in_v1 'without false capability claims'.

Six post-v1 capabilities carry complete closed refusal sets (81 classes) inside the v1 design gate. For #29, #30, #31 and #33 the matrix obligation before #39 was only to document that the capability is inactive, and #28 asked only for an explicit post-v1 contract, so this is design weight beyond what #39 asked for, although it is harmless if it is correctly labeled post-v1.

findings.what: The package (§1) and 02 §3 say the pinned patch series provides ADR-023 and ADR-025, but none of the 49 patches contains the signed UserDecisionRecord journal, the authority/dependency/intent/consumed-nonce/result/integration_authorization heads, authorityGuard, appendIntentEvent, gate-result receipts, orchestrateChildBatch or integrateApproved (grep finds 0 matches; 0023 signs a creation grant, not user authority), and REQUIRED_DAEMON_CAPABILITIES demands only `task.creation-binding` v2. So the stated fail-closed rule (04 ADR-001, README #16, 02 §3/§4: no model workflow unless all three primitives are loaded) is not what the preflight checks, and the whole user-authority and custody chain the design relies on has no mechanism on the daemon side of the boundary.

The only gate before the irreversible target-branch CAS (IntegrationAuthorizationRecord, protected integration_authorization_head, `integration_authorization_*` refusals) has no evaluator in src/ or in the patch series. The vocabulary records `integration_authorization_required` as producer=host with producer_files set to `scripts/validate-integration-authorization.mjs`, a script that validates the contract document. That lets the producer-missing check pass on a document validator (11 entries name a validate-* script as producer), and section 5 does not list this gap among what is not claimed.

findings.where: package §4 / §5 'What is not claimed' (17 contracts 'no link measured')
findings.what: The package leaves it to the seats to decide whether load-bearing contracts such as integration-authorization, material-decisions (the alignment projector gate), platform-support and sdk-write-api are unimplemented or only unlinked. Grepping src/ and compat/ for their refusal classes finds nothing, so at least these contracts are design obligations with no evaluator on either side of the host/daemon boundary.

The partition says family is 'a property of the model', yet it files the Meta models muse-spark-1.3 and muse-spark-1.3-contributor under the `kimi` family next to cursor-kimi-2.5. Cross-family independence, Lead selection and the master order GPT→Kimi→Grok→Opus (01 §3/§6) therefore rest on a vendor assignment that is factually wrong: a Kimi-authored artifact would exclude an unrelated Meta reviewer, and the intent seat reported as 'Kimi' is not Kimi.

The root of trust for every user-authority record is a probe that both documents say does not attest isolation, and platform attestation is deferred. This is disclosed honestly, but combined with the missing ADR-023 journal the user-authority guarantee currently has neither an enforced boundary nor a daemon-side mechanism.
The three crash-harness groups have no un-faulted control, so for them the package cannot show the guard is specific (disclosed).
